title: Pilot integration readiness for first 5 customer stories
creator: Amaya Chen
description:
Objective: Ensure our first five pilot customers can integrate Redwood Inference with predictable latency, clear rollback paths, and a tight feedback loop. This ticket owns the cross-functional readiness checklist, release notes coordination, and post-activation success evaluation for the initial pilot cohort.

Scope: onboarding orchestration for five signed pilots (mix of AI-native startups and one mid-market customer). Scope includes: finalizing pre-flight integration checklist, coordinating engineering release notes and breaking-change communication, preparing runbooks for SRE/Support, creating a lightweight success dashboard, and running two dry-run onboarding rehearsals with Solutions Engineering.

Key deliverables:
- Customer-specific integration checklists (API keys, VPC routing, model pinning guidance)
- Consolidated release notes and compatibility matrix for the pilot release
- Support + SRE runbooks for common failure modes and rollback steps
- Pilot success dashboard (latency, error rate, token cost delta, qualitative feedback score)
- Feedback intake pipeline: weekly digest to PM/Eng/Design and fast-path bug triage protocol

Stakeholders and owners:
- PM lead: Amaya Chen (owner of readiness schedule and acceptance)
- Solutions Eng: Priya Nanda (customer technical validation)
- Release Eng: Mateo Ruiz (release notes + compatibility matrix)
- SRE/Support: Kelsey Park (runbooks and pager routing)
- Design/UX: Noor Patel (feedback survey and onboarding UX tweaks)

Timeline and milestones:
- 2026-02-22: finalize customer-specific checklists (Done)
- 2026-03-03: release notes draft completed and shared with Eng (Done)
- 2026-03-08: dry-run #1 with Solutions Eng (observations captured)
- 2026-03-12: dry-run #2 with full on-call + support (scheduled)
- 2026-03-18: pilot ramp window opens for cohort A (soft-launch)
- 2026-03-25: pilot health review and go/no-go for broader activation

Communication plan:
- Weekly pilot sync (PM + SRE + SE + Release) every Monday at 09:30 PT
- Daily status channel in Slack: #pilot-activation (policy: update once per day if status changed)
- Release notes cadence: draft -> eng review -> legal/security sign-off -> customer-facing summary

Notes about release notes: coordinate with Release Eng to include a compatibility matrix showing model variants that are pinned vs. allowed to autoswitch, and explicit guidance on KV cache behavior and sequence-length implications for latency-sensitive customers. Customer-facing notes must include a short remediation checklist (how to pin older model, how to switch region, whom to call).

Success criteria (initial):
- All 5 pilots can perform a full smoke-test (generate + stream + structured output) within SLA (99th percentile latency under 350ms for prepared prompts)
- No critical production incidents during soft-launch window (no P0 incidents)
- Average pilot NPS-style feedback >= 7/10 at week 2 post-activation
- Observed token cost delta within projected estimate +/- 20%

acceptance_criteria: Checklist: each pilot completes API key + region + model pin steps and runs smoke tests without manual engineering intervention
Release notes: public-facing summary and internal compatibility matrix published and linked in the onboarding doc
Runbooks: SRE and Support runbooks validated in dry-run #2 and acknowledged by on-call rotation
Feedback loop: survey responses from at least 4/5 pilots and a compiled action list within 7 days
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected runtime kernel behavior at longer sequence lengths. Mitigation: include a conservative model pin recommendation and canary traffic routing for affected pilots.
Risk: Customer-facing release notes are too technical. Mitigation: produce both a short customer summary and an in-depth engineering appendix.
Risk: Pager fatigue for SRE. Mitigation: routing pilot alerts to a dedicated rotation and threshold tuning to avoid noisy alerts.
